sections.title: Recommendations: type 1 diabetes
rows: Treat most adults with T1D with CSII or MDI of prandial (injected or inhaled) plus basal insulin
Insulin analogs (or inhaled insulin) are preferred over injected human insulins to reduce hypoglycemia
Teach matching of mealtime insulin to carbohydrate (and fat/protein where needed), correction doses from current glucose and trends, sick-day rules and exercise adjustments
Reassess the insulin plan and insulin-taking behavior regularly (e.g., every 3–6 months)

sections.title: Recommendations: type 2 diabetes — choosing drugs by comorbidity
rows: Shared decision-making: efficacy plus CV, kidney, weight and comorbidity effects, hypoglycemia risk, cost and access, adverse effects, preferences
Consider combination therapy at initiation to reach goals sooner
Established or high risk of ASCVD: include a GLP-1 RA and/or SGLT2i with proven CV benefit, irrespective of A1C
HF (reduced or preserved EF): SGLT2i for glycemia and to prevent HF hospitalization, irrespective of A1C
T2D + obesity + symptomatic HFpEF: include tirzepatide (benefit on HF symptoms and events), irrespective of A1C
Same group: include a GLP-1 RA with proven benefit on HF symptoms (A) and/or HF events (B)

CKD (confirmed eGFR 20–60 and/or albuminuria): SGLT2i or GLP-1 RA with proven benefit, for glycemia, slowing CKD and fewer CV events, irrespective of A1C; SGLT2i glucose effect is smaller below eGFR 45
Advanced CKD (eGFR <30): GLP-1 RA preferred for glycemia (less hypoglycemia, CV benefit) (B); on dialysis, GLP-1-based therapy not cleared by the kidney can be started or continued (C)
MASLD with overweight/obesity: consider a GLP-1 RA with MASH benefit (A) or tirzepatide (potential benefit, B) for glycemia and as a weight-loss adjunct
Biopsy-proven MASH or high fibrosis risk on noninvasive tests: GLP-1 RA preferred (A); pioglitazone or tirzepatide can be considered (B)
Same group: pioglitazone + GLP-1 RA combination can be considered

sections.title: Recommendations: type 2 diabetes — reassessment, intensification and insulin
rows: Reassess the medication plan and medication-taking behavior every 3–6 months
Do not delay intensification or deintensification when goals are not met
Base changes on glycemic and weight goals, comorbidities (CV, kidney, liver, metabolic) and hypoglycemia risk
When starting a new drug, reassess need for and dose of sulfonylureas, meglitinides and insulin
Do not combine a DPP-4 inhibitor with a GLP-1 RA or tirzepatide (no added glucose lowering)
Weight goals not met: add weight-management measures (lifestyle intensification, structured programs, drugs, metabolic surgery)
Consider insulin, whatever the background therapy, if hyperglycemic symptoms or A1C >10% (>86 mmol/mol) or glucose ≥300 mg/dL (≥16.7 mmol/L)
Without severe hyperglycemia or crisis, GLP-1-based therapy is preferred to insulin as initial or add-on therapy
If insulin is used, combine it with a GLP-1 RA or tirzepatide; reassess insulin dose when these are added or escalated
When starting insulin, continue other glucose-lowering drugs (unless contraindicated or not tolerated) for weight, cardiometabolic and kidney benefits

sections.title: Recommendations: all people with diabetes — technology, glucagon, cost, shortages

Offer AID to all adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes on insulin, per needs and preferences

If a drug is unavailable (e.g., shortage), switch to another FDA-approved drug of similar efficacy

SAVOR-TIMI 53 (saxagliptin HF signal); TECOS; CARMELINA; EXAMINE
Reduces CV mortality vs sulfonylurea as first line
sections.note: MACE/HF/kidney labels follow ADA Table 9.2. Trial figures are not given here on purpose (several ADA trial numbers differ from the papers; items key on ADA's clinical conclusion). SGLT2i + GLP-1 RA together may be considered for additive CV and kidney benefit (Rec 10.40d, B).

sections.title: Special situations: what to use
rows: Add a second (barrier) method or switch to non-oral contraception
Relying on the pill alone while starting or escalating
ADA: until the maintenance dose is reached and used ≥4 weeks; label: 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase. GLP-1 RAs affect pill levels less
Insulin-based plan; reach preconception glycemic goals over several months
Noninsulin drugs with unknown or known pregnancy risk
Use contraception while on such drugs. Stop semaglutide ≥2 months before planned conception (Section 15 / US label); ADA gives no US interval for tirzepatide
Insulin; consider basal insulin if glucose >250 mg/dL (>13.9 mmol/L) while evaluating
Stopping the ICI (β-cell loss is irreversible)
Onset 1 week to 12 months; incidence ≤1%; often abrupt DKA; prandial insulin if insulinopenic; usually lifelong insulin
Insulin and sulfonylureas (last resort: insulin may reactivate PI3K signaling); GLP-1 RA not advised
Onset within 2 weeks, ~60% incidence; risk: prediabetes, BMI >25, age >65. Pioglitazone an option; SGLT2i effective but watch for ketoacidosis
Pioglitazone second line; GLP-1 RA or SGLT2i possible on overall risk–benefit; insulin for refractory or severe cases
Insulin matched to steroid timing; NPH given in the morning with morning prednisone
Checking only fasting glucose (misses the afternoon–evening peak)

Prednisone: glucose rises after the first meal, peaks afternoon/evening, back to baseline by morning; dexamethasone can raise glucose >24 h. Reduce insulin as the steroid tapers; other oral drugs only for stable chronic doses
Incretins (GLP-1 RA, tirzepatide, DPP-4i) after pancreatitis
No interactions with transplant drugs; may help prevent PTDM. DPP-4i for mild hyperglycemia; sulfonylureas possible with stable kidney function
Noninsulin drugs; GLP-1 RA often preferred (Rec 9.38b)
Metformin: not started at eGFR <45, stop <30 (graft dysfunction → lactic acidosis risk)
SGLT2i for ASCVD/HF/CKD but higher UTI risk after kidney transplant (stent); GLP-1 RA: no immunosuppressant interaction, watch GI effects; gastroparesis/reflux a concern in lung transplant
OGTT preferred over A1C or FPG
Pretransplant OGTT on the waitlist, at ~3 months and from 1 year after transplant (2024 international consensus)
May later need insulin; HNF1A: adding a DPP-4i may help
INS, GATA6, EIF2AK3, FOXP3 mutations need insulin (ADA prints 'KCNJ22', a typo)
Education, ketone (serum β-hydroxybutyrate) testing, sick-day plan
Ketogenic diets, prolonged fasting, dehydration, alcohol; any prior DKA
Rec 9.39; hold before surgery, in acute illness and prolonged fasting
sections.note: Glucose conversions: 250 mg/dL = 13.9 mmol/L. MODY and neonatal details link to ADA Section 2 (classification). The 2-month semaglutide washout comes from Section 15 and the US label.

sections.title: Cross-references that drive drug choice (Sections 5, 6, 8, 10, 11)
rows: Before religious fasting (e.g., Ramadan) generate an IDF-DAR risk score with the updated pre-fasting assessment; give fasting-focused education
Optimize plan, doses and timing well before fasting to avoid hypoglycemia, dehydration, hyperglycemia and ketoacidosis
A1C goal <7% (<53 mmol/mol) for many nonpregnant adults without significant hypoglycemia
Time in range >70% for many adults using CGM
Time <70 mg/dL (<3.9 mmol/L) <4% (<1% in older adults); time <54 mg/dL (<3.0 mmol/L) <1%; deintensify if not met
Lower goal (e.g., <6.5% [<48 mmol/mol]) if healthy with low treatment risk and burden
Less stringent goals with cognitive/functional limits, frailty, severe comorbidity, or when harms outweigh benefits
T2D with overweight/obesity: prioritize glucose-lowering drugs that lower weight
Consider obesity pharmacotherapy together with lifestyle change
Preferred obesity drugs: semaglutide or tirzepatide (greatest weight loss plus weight-independent benefits)
Consider metabolic surgery in T2D with BMI ≥30.0 kg/m² (≥27.5 in Asian American people) if a good surgical candidate
T1D with obesity: GLP-1 RA-based therapy (B) and metabolic surgery (C) as in the general population
Established ASCVD or CKD: SGLT2i or GLP-1 RA with proven CV benefit
ASCVD, multiple risk factors or CKD: SGLT2i with proven CV benefit
Same groups: GLP-1 RA with proven CV benefit
ASCVD or multiple risk factors: SGLT2i plus GLP-1 RA may be considered for additive benefit
Established HF (HFpEF or HFrEF): SGLT2i (including SGLT1/2i) with proven benefit to cut worsening HF and CV death
Same: SGLT2i with proven benefit to improve quality of life
CKD with albuminuria on maximal ACEi/ARB: nonsteroidal MRA with proven CV and kidney benefit
Stage B HF, or high risk of / established CVD: SGLT inhibitor (A) or GLP-1 RA (B) with HF-prevention benefit
T2D + obesity + symptomatic HFpEF: tirzepatide (A) or GLP-1 RA (B) with benefit on HF events
Same group: tirzepatide or GLP-1 RA with benefit on HF symptoms
T2D + CKD: nonsteroidal MRA with proven benefit to reduce HF hospitalization
Stable HF: metformin may continue if eGFR >30; avoid in unstable or hospitalized HF
Same as Rec 9.39: DKA education and ketone testing with SGLT inhibition
ACEi or ARB to maximally tolerated dose for UACR 30–299 mg/g (B); strongly for UACR ≥300 mg/g and/or eGFR <60 (A)
T2D + CKD: SGLT2i with proven benefit; start at eGFR ≥20 and can continue until kidney failure
T2D + CKD: GLP-1 RA with proven benefit to slow CKD and reduce CV risk
CKD with albuminuria: nonsteroidal MRA (finerenone) if eGFR ≥25; check potassium 1 month after starting
SGLT2i and finerenone can be started together if UACR ≥100 mg/g and eGFR 30–90 on a RAS inhibitor
Avoid kidney-protective drugs harmful in pregnancy without reliable contraception; switch before conception
sections.note: SGLT2 inhibitors, ACEi/ARB, MRAs and neprilysin inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy (Section 11).

sections.title: Ramadan fasting: IDF-DAR 2021 dose adjustments (with ADA Section 5 contrast)

Hypoglycemia unawareness; eGFR <30; unstable macrovascular disease

Finger-prick testing and insulin injections do not break the fast
No dose change: once daily at iftar; twice daily at iftar and suhoor; three times daily: morning dose before suhoor, afternoon dose added to iftar

Use gliclazide (MR) or glimepiride; once daily at iftar (reduce if well controlled); twice daily: iftar dose unchanged, reduce suhoor dose. Avoid glibenclamide (dose reduction did not lower hypoglycemia)

Redistribute three meal doses to the two meals by meal size

No change once titration is complete; finish titration at least 2–4 weeks before Ramadan
No dose change; take at iftar or suhoor
Basal insulin, once daily (NPH, glargine, degludec, glargine-300)

Table 5.4: reduce 25–35% if not well managed; no timing change for glargine-300/degludec
Usual morning dose at iftar; evening dose halved and taken at suhoor
Normal dose at iftar; omit lunch dose; reduce suhoor dose by 25–50%
Table 5.4: reduce the pre-fast meal dose 35–50%
Once daily: normal dose at iftar. Twice daily: usual morning dose at iftar, suhoor dose reduced 20–50%. Three times daily: omit the afternoon dose
Reduce insulin ~25–50% by risk score and reduce the SU
<70 mg/dL (<3.9 mmol/L) or symptoms: −4 U; <90 mg/dL (<5.0 mmol/L): −2 U; 90–126 mg/dL (5.0–7.0 mmol/L): no change; >126 mg/dL (>7.0 mmol/L): +2 U; >200 mg/dL (>11.1 mmol/L): +4 U
Basal −30–40% at iftar; rapid analog: suhoor −30–50%, skip lunch, iftar dose by 2-h post-iftar glucose
Basal −20–40% in the last 3–4 h of the fast; increase modestly early after iftar
sections.note: ADA Section 9 itself does not discuss Ramadan. Every Ramadan dose item names IDF-DAR 2021. Glucose conversions are by arithmetic (300 mg/dL = 16.7, 200 mg/dL = 11.1 mmol/L); IDF-DAR prints 16.6 and mislabels 200 mg/dL as 16.7, so items never hinge on these printed values. Saudi validation data: more than half of high-risk people fasted anyway.
